newsitem.title: CANADA: QLT expects to erase losses next year.
newsitem.headline: QLT expects to erase losses next year.

text.p: Biotechnology company QLT PhotoTherapeutics Inc said Monday that it expects to be close to break-even in 1998 and report a profit in 1999.

"We're hoping that next year we'll see very close to break even and then it (a profit) will be the following year... That's reasonable," Chief Executive Julia Levy told reporters at QLT's annual meeting.
She said the company's exact performance depended on several variables including when drugs in its pipeline are rolled out.
QLT, which lost C$4.7 million or C$0.19 a share in 1996, is commercializing a light-activated treatment for cancer and other diseases.

QLT generated its first revenues from sales of its light-activated drug Photofrin in 1996, a landmark that chairman Duff Scott said signalled its transformation from a development-stage to commercial company.

Levy anticipated a "very rapid ramp-up in revenues" when the company launches its drug BPD for ocular applications. A Phase Three clinical trial is underway testing BPD for the treatment of an eye condition known as age-related macular degeneration, the leading cause of blindness in the elderly.
QLT plans to submit an approval application to regulators in the United States and Europe for BPD use with macular degeneration in late 1998 or early 1999 and aims for a commerical launch in 1999.

It hopes to receive approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration late this year or early next year for use of Photofrin for lung cancer. Levy said the company expects to meet with an FDA panel in September. Photofrin currently only has U.S. approval for use in esophogeal cancer.
QLT also plans clinical trials of Photofrin for Barrett's Esophoagus, a precancerous condition, this year.

The company is holding talks toward negotiating an alliance with a major pharmaceutical company for oncology marketing in Asia outside Japan. An announcement is likely late this year but QLT officials would not disclose potential partners.
Levy told shareholders that 1997 looks "very promising" for the biotechnology sector. She hoped this would translate into continued strong performance of the company's stock.
Many of the submissions pending from more than 20 biotechnology companies are expected to recieve U.S. regulatory approval which will help draw investor attention to the sector, she said.
QLT is among the 25 biggest biotech stocks in North America based on market capitalization, she said.
